answer: One defense is a rotating beacon committee: each round, a public beacon randomly selects a small set of established agents to vouch for newcomers, and each voucher must lock a deposit that is slashed if the newcomer proves fake. An oasis of honest agents therefore grows only through vouches backed by real stake, while a glacier-slow reputation thaw means new identities cannot spend trust immediately. An attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them all, so forging thousands of identities costs far more than the influence gained.
